entries.title: Country packs: GDPR, UK and Australia
entries.detail: Data protection requirements now sit alongside the core frameworks, grouped by lifecycle gate with their sources. GDPR is added automatically when the system has an EU connection and processes personal data (lawful basis, transparency, DPIA, Art. 22 automated decisions, data protection by design, processors and transfers, security). Selecting the UK adds UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, including the new Articles 22A-22D in force since 5 February 2026, and ICO guidance. Selecting Australia adds the Privacy Act and APPs, including the automated-decision privacy policy rules (APP 1.7-1.9) from 10 December 2026, OAIC guidance and the national Guidance for AI Adoption. All checked against primary legislation.

entries.title: ISO/IEC references verified
entries.detail: Every ISO/IEC 42001, 23894 and 42005 reference was checked against NIST's official crosswalks from the AI RMF to those standards, and the 42001 controls against a listing of the published edition. References now show their clause or control title, ISO/IEC 42005 is cited by clause, and a few missing references were added. First-action text no longer shows internal codes.

entries.title: Baseline v2: purpose-first EU AI Act classification
entries.detail: The Baseline has been rebuilt. You now describe an AI use case by its intended purpose, your role and its impact, and get: its EU AI Act classification, working through Art. 2 scope, Art. 5 prohibitions, Annex I, Annex III and the Art. 6(3) exemption, Art. 50 transparency and Art. 25 role shifts, with the reasoning shown; a governance tier from 1 to 4; requirements by lifecycle gate, crosswalked to ISO/IEC 42001, 23894 and 42005 and the NIST AI RMF and Generative AI Profile; your first five actions; and the open questions to escalate. The rules were checked against the Official Journal text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and 2026/1744 and are tested against a public suite of legal scenarios. This fixes the known classification errors listed below. Coverage now focuses on the EU AI Act, ISO/IEC and NIST: the Australian, UK, GDPR, APRA and OWASP mappings from the earlier version are retired, with optional country packs planned. Links shared from the earlier version no longer open a result; please answer the new questions.

entries.title: Known issue: EU AI Act classification is being rebuilt
entries.detail: A review found that this version classifies systems by technology rather than intended purpose. That causes known errors: fraud detection shown as high-risk under Annex III 5(b), despite being carved out; workplace emotion recognition not flagged as prohibited under Article 5(1)(f); credit scoring by an LLM not shown as high-risk; Annex III education, biometric, law-enforcement, migration and justice uses not mapped; and general-purpose AI model duties listed for deployers. Don't rely on this version to decide whether a system is prohibited or high-risk. Version 2, built around purpose, role and impact and checked against the Official Journal text, is in progress: see the project README on GitHub.

entries.title: EU AI Act dates updated for the Digital Omnibus
entries.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force on 27 July 2026. Annex III high-risk obligations (Articles 9–15, 26, 27, 86) now show as applying from 2 December 2027 and medical-device AI from 2 August 2028; since 2 August 2026 they had incorrectly shown as in force. GPAI model obligations corrected to 2 August 2025 and reframed as provider duties. Article 4 AI literacy wording updated.

entries.title: New mappings: EU transparency, new prohibitions, OWASP agentic
entries.detail: Added EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations (in force 2 August 2026) for chatbots, agents, generative and biometric systems; the new Article 5 prohibitions on non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM generation (from 2 December 2026); and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for agentic systems.

entries.title: Australian and UK mappings refreshed
entries.detail: The AU Voluntary AI Safety Standard is replaced by the Guidance for AI Adoption (6 essential practices, October 2025). The Privacy Act automated decision-making mapping now reflects OAIC guidance (APP 1.7–1.9 from 10 December 2026) and also applies to decision-support systems. The UK mapping reflects UK GDPR Articles 22A–22D, in force since 5 February 2026. OWASP LLM Top 10 references updated to the 2026 edition (Excessive Agency is now LLM03; System Prompt Leakage is now Hidden Context Exposure, LLM08).

entries.title: Automatic check for regulatory dates passing
entries.detail: A scheduled check now flags any mapping whose effective date passes after it was last verified, so date changes like the Digital Omnibus are caught for review.

entries.title: Provenance icons, framework version footers, and changelog shipped
entries.detail: Every regulatory item, control, and risk now surfaces its source note and last-verified date via a (?) icon. Framework versions are explicit in the Regulatory drill. Changelog route added at /changelog.
